## Overview

 [![247px-Gold seal policy.svg](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/6/69/247px-Gold_seal_policy.svg.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/140?cb=20160101093814)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/6/69/247px-Gold_seal_policy.svg.png/revision/latest?cb=20160101093814) 



 

**Social Policies** refer to guidelines, principles, legislation and activities that affect the living conditions of your nation's citizens. Important areas of social policy are well-being and welfare, poverty reduction, social security, justice, unemployment insurance, living conditions, animal rights, pensions, health care, social housing, family policy, social care, child protection, social exclusion, education policy, crime and criminal justice, urban development, and labor issues.

A nation's Social Policies are determined by an [in-game questionnaire](https://politicsandwar.com/nation/policy/) which rates responses on a scale from anarchist to fascist. These social polices are entirely cosmetic, and have no effect on the game.

## Social Policies Rating

## Overview

 [![Pen-policy](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/bb/Pen-policy.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/286?cb=20170517121921)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/bb/Pen-policy.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170517121921) 



 

**Policies** (or National Policies) are a role-playing mechanic.

There are two kinds of National Policies: "[Social Policies](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Social_Policies) " and "[Economic Policies](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Economic_Policies)". Each of these has an overal rating displayed on your nation page based on your answers to an [in-game questionare](https://politicsandwar.com/nation/policy/).

Neither kind of policies has any impact on your nation mechanically, so there is no 'best' setting. The default value for both policies is "Moderate".

## The Questionnaire

In order to define your social and economic policies ratings, you have to answer to questions related to:

:   Cannabis, Mandatory Service, Capital Punishment, Secondary Education, Prohibition, Energy, Assisted Suicide, Same-Sex Marriage, Unions, Campaign Finance, Speech, Hard Drugs, Spending, Infant Circumcision, Immigration, Gun Rights, Religion, Healthcare, Polygamist Marriage, Taxes, Torture, Abortion, Welfare.

Once you select your answers and submit them, a quick calculation is made to determine your social and economic policies. **No information about your answers is stored**, so neither you or anybody else is able to see your answers. If you fill out the answers and still have "Moderate" Social and Economic Policies, it's because your answers determined your nation has moderate policies. Your answers to the questions are not displayed publicly. Only the overall result of your survey is shown on your nation page.

## Overview

Although there are no default religions to choose from, it is possible to define the name as well as the symbol of the religion you want your nation to follow. Currently, there are 24 standard religious symbols to choose from, while it is possible for VIP players to add icons of their own.

You can change your State Religion whenever you want. To do that:

1. On the left-side navigation bar click "Edit" under the "Nation" heading.
2. Next to "Religion", there is a drop down box from which you can select the religious symbol you prefer. You can also type the name of the religion you want to adopt.
3. Scroll to the bottom and click the "Edit Nation" button.

title: Aircraft
content:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Tools blue.svg](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/2/2d/Tools_blue.svg.png/revision/latest?cb=20150213023616) | This page is about game mechanics. This page is about game mechanics. It contains information such as formulas, costs, & other miscellany. See [Category:Mechanics](/wiki/Category:Mechanics "Category:Mechanics") for other pages on game mechanics. |

## Overview

 [![Airforcesmall](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/6/6a/Airforcesmall.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/220?cb=20150411061530)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/6/6a/Airforcesmall.png/revision/latest?cb=20150411061530) 



 

**Aircraft** (commonly referred to as Planes) are used in [Airstrikes](/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike") both offensively and defensively. They are excellent at destroying [infrastructure](/wiki/Infrastructure "Infrastructure") and other military units. They are the only military unit that can attack other military units: Aircraft can kill [Soldiers](/wiki/Soldiers "Soldiers") and destroy [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") and [Ships](/wiki/Naval_Ships "Naval Ships"), as well as other Aircraft. Aircraft do **not** destroy improvements.

Aircraft can also be used for getting Air Superiority, which decreases the efficiency (their power in battle, not their numbers) of enemy [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") by 50%.

Aircraft are also affected by Ground Control. Once Ground Control has been established, all subsequent Ground Battles will destroy some of your opponent's Aircraft (based on the number of [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") you send in battle).

To build Aircraft you need to build Hangars in your cities (which must be powered). Each Hangar allows you to produce 3 Aircraft per day and can host 15 Aircraft in total.

## Cost, Upkeep and Required Resources

Each Aircraft costs $4,000 and 5 Aluminum [![Aluminum](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/ba/Aluminum.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416044855)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Aluminum"). It also has a daily upkeep cost of $500 during peace time and $750 during war time.

Aircraft require both Munitions [![Munitions](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Munitions") and Gasoline [![Gasoline](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Gasoline") to operate. By default, Aircraft will arm themselves with any available Munitions [![Munitions](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Munitions") and Gasoline [![Gasoline](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Gasoline"). Any Aircraft without Munitions [![Munitions](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Munitions") or Gasoline [![Gasoline](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Gasoline") will not participate in fighting (either offensive or defensive). In case you do not have enough Munitions [![Munitions](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Munitions") or Gasoline [![Gasoline](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Gasoline") to use all of your Aircraft during an offensive [Airstrike](/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike") you launch, a notification will appear. 1 Munition [![Munitions](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Munitions") and 1 Gasoline [![Gasoline](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Gasoline") are required for every 4 Aircraft.

## Aircraft Capacity

Aircraft are supported by Hangars which are military city improvements. Each Hangar can support a maximum of 15 Aircraft, and allows you to manufacture up to 3 Aircraft per day.

### Population Support

Maximum Aircraft capacity is also limited by a nation's population. Your maximum Aircraft count cannot exceed 0.1% of your nation's [population](/wiki/Population "Population"), regardless of how many Hangars you have.

## Strategic Use

Aircraft are considered the most powerful units of the game. They are excellent at destroying [infrastructure](/wiki/Infrastructure "Infrastructure") (much better than [Soldiers](/wiki/Soldiers "Soldiers") and [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") are) and pretty much all other units: Aircraft destroy [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") better than [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") destroy [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") during [Ground Battles](/wiki/Ground_Battles "Ground Battles") and [Ships](/wiki/Naval_Ships "Naval Ships") better than [Ships](/wiki/Naval_Ships "Naval Ships") destroy [Ships](/wiki/Naval_Ships "Naval Ships") during [Naval Battles](/wiki/Naval_Battle "Naval Battle"). The damage depends on the number of Aircraft sent for an [Airstrike](/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike"). For this reason, many nations and alliances try to keep maximum airforce.

Aircraft have been nerfed in the 14 May 2020 update:

* [Soldiers](/wiki/Soldiers "Soldiers") Killed [Airstrike](/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike"): 43% -> 25%
* [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") Killed [Airstrike](/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike"): 43% -> 14%
* [Ships](/wiki/Naval_Ships "Naval Ships") Killed [Airstrike](/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike"): 41% -> 34%
* Aircraft Killed [Airstrike](/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike")(Dogfight): 83% -> 53%
* Aircraft Killed by [Tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") in a [Ground Battle](/wiki/Ground_Battles "Ground Battles"): 0% -> 42% (only after Ground Control has been established)

title: Population Density
content:
Population Density is the average number of people per square mile.

## Importance

Population Density is an important factor in controlling [disease](/wiki/Disease "Disease"). The higher a nation's Population Density, the higher the disease rate (which will lower the nation's actual [population](/wiki/Population "Population"), lowering gross income).

Recommended Population Density for each city is 50 people per square mile unless a hospital is present in that city.

## Overview

 [![Infrastructure](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/0/03/Infrastructure.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/270?cb=20170602075720)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/0/03/Infrastructure.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170602075720) 



 

Infrastructure is the basic foundation of a city. It increases the Base Population of a city and allows more Improvements to be constructed. Infrastructure becomes 5% cheaper with the [Center for Civil Engineering](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Center_for_Civil_Engineering) project.

## Relation to Population

Infrastructure directly affects the base population by increasing it at a maximum of 100 people per 1 infrastructure. The formula is:

```
Base Population = Infrastructure * 100
```

## Cost Per Level

Infrastructure cost follows an exponential curve. Interestingly enough, the cheapest infrastructure available is not at zero infrastructure.

```
Cost Per Level = 300+[(Infrastructure-10)^2.2]/710
```

**Arms Stockpile** is a [National Project](/wiki/National_Project "National Project") that boosts [Munitions Factories](/wiki/Improvements/Manufacturing "Improvements/Manufacturing")' productivity by 34% nationwide. Rates increase from 1.5/turn (per Munitions Factory) to 2.01/turn (per Munitions Factory). Lead usage is increased accordingly to create more Munitions.

This project costs 125 Aluminum [![Aluminum](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/ba/Aluminum.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416044855)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Aluminum"), 125 Steel [![Steel](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/c/c9/Steel.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416051706)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Steel") and $4,000,000.

## Overview

Orbis is the world on which the ongoing political and military struggles documented on [Politics and War](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Politics_and_War_Wiki) occur.

Orbis may refer not only to the virtual in-game world, but also to the [roleplay world](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Orbis_Cosmology) created by the community.

The name of the world was chosen by the P&W community itself. Through the [Orbis World Forum](https://politicsandwar.com/forums/), the very first inhabitants of this virtual world proposed several names and voted on them. The winning name "Orbis" was proposed by [Sheepy](/wiki/Sheepy "Sheepy") who was inspired by the latin word "[orbis](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/orbis)", meaning (along other things) "world" or "Earth".

## Orbis Date, Seasons, Time, Turns and Activity

 [![OrbisDate](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/2/24/OrbisDate.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170519110222)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/2/24/OrbisDate.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170519110222) 



 

Information provided:

* Real Date: e.g. May 19 (2017)
* Orbis Date: e.g. April 13 2016 (it differs from the Real Date)
* Weather icon: e.g. Cloudy = Spring: Normal food production
* [Orbis Time](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/timezone/utc): e.g. 10:35 am (time in [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time) )
* Next turn in: e.g. 1:25 (1 hour and 25 minutes)
* Players Online: e.g. 72

The seasons in the Northern Hemisphere run as follows: Dec-Feb (Winter), Mar-May (Spring), Jun-Aug (Summer), and Sep-Nov (Fall). In the Southern Hemisphere they are reversed.

Each turn lasts for 2 hours, resulting in 12 turns per day.

title: Arable Land Agency
content:
[![Arable land agency](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/1/18/Arable_land_agency.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20210111063741)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/1/18/Arable_land_agency.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20210111063741) 



 

**Arable Land Agency** is a [National Project](/wiki/National_Project "National Project") that makes it easier and more cost effective to acquire new habitable [land](/wiki/Land "Land"), reducing the cost of purchasing new land in [cities](/wiki/City "City") by 5%. This project is a pre-requisite for [Advanced Engineering Corps](/wiki/Advanced_Engineering_Corps "Advanced Engineering Corps").

This project costs 1,500 Coal [![Coal](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/a/a7/Coal.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416051040)](/wiki/Resources#Natural_Resources "Coal"), 1,500 Lead [![Lead](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/e/e8/Lead.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416051319)](/wiki/Resources#Natural_Resources "Lead") and $3,000,000.

title: Advanced Urban Planning
content:
[![Advancedcityplanning](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/9/9b/Advancedcityplanning.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20190519073451)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/9/9b/Advancedcityplanning.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20190519073451) 



 

**Advanced Urban Planning** is a [National Project](/wiki/National_Project "National Project") that reduces the cost of building new [cities](/wiki/City "City") by $100,000,000 per city. It requires 16 cities and [Urban Planning](/wiki/Urban_Planning "Urban Planning") to build. The cost reduction provided by this national project stacks with Urban Planning for a total reduction of $150,000,000.

The cost of this project is 10,000 Uranium [![Uranium](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/3/31/Uranium.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416051754)](/wiki/Resources#Natural_Resources "Uranium"), 40,000 Aluminum [![Aluminum](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/ba/Aluminum.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416044855)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Aluminum"), 20,000 Steel [![Steel](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Steel"), 20,000 Munitions [![Munitions](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Munitions") and 2,500,000 Food [![Food](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Natural_Resources "Food").

## Overview

**Currency** is an option you are able to pick in order to define the system of money (monetary units) that your nation adopts for actual use or circulation (as a medium of exchange). This option does not provide any nation bonuses and exists merely for role-playing reasons.

To change your Currency:

1. On the left-side navigation bar click "Edit" under the "Nation" heading.
2. Next to "Currency", there is a drop-down box. Select the currency you wish to use.
3. Scroll to the bottom & click the "Edit Nation" button.

You can change your Currency whenever you want.

The **Dvinmiste Capia Armed Forces** have many uniform base on their ranking places, his soldiers are fanatically loyal to **[Zenya Kurtarov](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Zenya_Kurtarov)** and share his deep dislike of **Russia**. They attack with a variety of weapons, including but not limited to pistols, machetes, rifles, and a variety of explosives. They also follow the basic guerrilla infantry rule - they're not too smart, or too much of a threat in small numbers, but they can be a real headache if there are a few dozen attacking from various flanks.

## **Dvinmiste Capia Army**

The **[Dvinmiste Capia Army](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Dvinmiste_Capia_Army?action=create)** (**DCA**) is the [land warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_warfare) service branch of the Dvinmiste Capia Armed Forces. As a branch of the armed forces, the mission of the D.C. Army is "to fight and win our Nation's wars, by providing prompt, sustained, land dominance, across the full range of military operations and the spectrum of conflict, in support of combatant commanders". The branch is the major ground-based offensive and defensive force of the **Armed Republic of Dvinmiste Capia**.

### **Dvinmiste Capia Blue Berets Divition**

The **[Blue Berets Divition](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Blue_Berets_Divition)**  are elite military units trained to conduct special operations such as police raids to military operations in internal conflicts. Coverage of these operations, and the celebrity status of special operations forces in state-controlled media, encouraged the public to identify many of these forces by name: **DCBBD**or just **BBD**.

### **Vehicles**

* [![Standard MV-280A](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/d/d9/MV-280A.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20180617070329)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/d/d9/MV-280A.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180617070329) 

  Standard MV-280A

   The army's most common vehicle is the **MV-280A**, which is capable of serving as a cargo/troop carrier, weapons platform and ambulance, among many other roles. The MV-280A was originally designed to evacuate and transport soldiers from combat faster and with greater efficiency. In some instances, they also used to transport weapons and ammunition for light artillery and infantry purposes. When Capian engineers observed the efficiency of the speed of the MV-280A, they decided make a new model to support tanks. The light artillery **MV-280B** armed with an R/C 105 mm anti-vehicle rocket rack, and the **MV-280C** armed with an HMG-15 7.92mm eventually replaced the A variant.

* [![Standard Landseek](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/b5/Landseek.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20180617070718)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/b5/Landseek.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180617070718) 

  Standard Landseek

   The **Landseek** is another common vehicle, is a transport used to carry enemy troops to the battlefield. It also has the capability to transport heavy artillery, such as tanks, AA-Guns and other armored vehicles. It is mainly used as a cheaper way to transport large amount of troops.

The Mammoth Tank was designed to go toe-to-toe with any enemy unit, and emerge the last unit standing.

## **Capian Air Force**

The **Capian Air Force** (**CAF**) is the [aerial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_warfare) and [space warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_warfare) service branch of the Dvinmiste Capia Armed Forces. Initially established as a part of the Dvinmiste Capia Army, the CAF was formed as a separate branch of the D.C. Armed Forces on 21 May with the passing of the **National Security Act of 2029**. It is the youngest branch of the D.C. Armed Forces, and the fourth in order of precedence. The CAF is one of the most largest air force in the region. The CAF articulates its core missions as [air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_supremacy) and [space superiority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_warfare), [global integrated ISR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence,_surveillance,_target_acquisition,_and_reconnaissance), [rapid global mobility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airlift), [global strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_bombing), and [command and control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_and_control). Along with conducting independent air and space operations, the Capian Air Force provides [air support](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_support) for land and naval forces and aids in the recovery of troops in the field.

### **Training**

All enlisted Airmen attend Basic Capian Military Training (BCMT) at Lortarov Air Force Base in Novaya for 8 1/2 weeks. Individuals who have prior service of over 24 months of active duty in the other service branches who seek to enlist in the Air Force must go through a 10-day Air Force familiarization course rather than enlisted BCMT, however prior service opportunities are severely limited.

Officers may be commissioned upon graduation from the Dvinmiste Capia Air Force Academy, upon graduation from another college or university through the Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps (AFROTC) program, or through the Air Force Officer Training School (OTS). OTS, located at Turov Air Force Base in Zeranya, in turn encompasses two separate commissioning programs: Basic Officer Training (BOT), which is for officer candidates for the Regular Air Force and the Air Force Reserve; and the Capian Academy of Military Science (CAMS), which is for officer candidates of the Air National Guard.

The CAF also provides Commissioned Officer Training (COT) for officers of all three components who are direct-commissioned into medicine, law, religion, biological sciences, or healthcare administration. COT is fully integrated into the OTS program and today encompasses extensive coursework as well as field exercises in leadership, confidence, fitness, and deployed-environment operations.

### **Air Force Fitness Test**

The Dvinmiste Capia Air Force Fitness Test (AFFT) is designed to test the abdominal circumference, muscular strength/endurance and cardiovascular respiratory fitness of airmen in the CAF. As part of the *Fit to Fight* program, the CAF adopted a more stringent physical fitness assessmen. In the AFFT, Airmen are given a score based on performance consisting of four components: waist circumference, the sit-up, the push-up, and a 1.5-mile (2.4 km) run. Airmen can potentially earn a score of 100, with the run counting as 60%, waist circumference as 20%, and both strength test counting as 10% each. A passing score is 75 points. The AFFT is administered by the base Capian Fitness Assessment Cell (CFAC), and is required twice a year. Personnel may test once a year if he or she earns a score above a 90%. Additionally, only meeting the minimum standards on each one of these tests will not get you a passing score of 75%, and failing any one component will result in a failure for the entire test.

### **Aircraft**

The various aircraft of the Air Force include:

* [![Jimki-B](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/0/0b/Jimki-B.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180625223951) [![Jimki-B](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/0/0b/Jimki-B.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20180625223951)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/0/0b/Jimki-B.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180625223951) 

  Jimki-B

   The **Jimki-B** is an [carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier)[-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-based_aircraft) [air-to-ground fighter aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_aircraft), fast and versatile. They carry self-propelled-heat-seeking bombs and machine guns which serves as their main firepower.

Zorak-15K

 

* The **Zorak ZiG-15K** is a [all-weather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_fighter) [carrier-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-based_aircraft) [multirole fighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multirole_combat_aircraft) aircraft developed by the [Zorak design bureau](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Zorak_design_bureau). Zorak describes it as a [4++ generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth-generation_jet_fighter) aircraft.

* [![C8A-Flyer](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/d/d2/DC-Flyer.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180625053013) [![C8A-Flyer](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/d/d2/DC-Flyer.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20180625053013)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/d/d2/DC-Flyer.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180625053013) 

  C8A-Flyer

   The **Khirkash** **CA8-Flyer** is a single-engine [ground-attack aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground-attack_aircraft). While it possesses excellent maneuverability due to its **V/STOL** capabilities, its rotary cannons have limited range, capable only of firing in an arc in front of the plane. It is also equipped with air-to-air AIM-9A Sidewinder missiles that, while being powerful, take some time to accelerate after being deployed.

* The **Khirkash D-72 Kuslov** is a jet-powered [strategic bomber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_bomber) and long-range gunship meant to provide close air support to ground troops. It is equipped with anti-air guns on its wings and can drop heavy bombs, and its size is enough to carry support tanks on its wings, is also capable of using its jet engines to burn anything underneath it.

* + ![D-72 Kuslov]()

    D-72 Kuslov
  + ![Brosky CBR-1]()

    Brosky CBR-1

  1/2

  The **Brosky CBR-1** was a Capian multi-purpose (including reconnaissance) [flying boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_boat) which entered service with the Capian Navy in 2029. In Dvinmiste Capia it sometimes carried the nickname of "Kорова" (cow).

* [![R-Zerik](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/8/85/R-Zerik.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180617070802) [![R-Zerik](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/8/85/R-Zerik.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20180617070802)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/8/85/R-Zerik.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180617070802) 

  R-Zerik

   The **Khirkash R-Zerik** is the main attack helicopter of the Capian Army. They are very fast, attacking by dropping bombs on ground targets or using rockets for aerial targets. They are often used to carry letters from soldiers or other people.

* [![MH-3R Valerian](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/e/e3/MH-3R_Zanheed.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180617070752) [![MH-3R Valerian](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/e/e3/MH-3R_Zanheed.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20180617070752)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/e/e3/MH-3R_Zanheed.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180617070752)

   The  **Khirkash MH-3R** **Valerian** are light utility helicopters, they are fast, cheap, reliable, and can pepper the enemy with their miniguns. They usually work in packs in the battlefield. Occasionally, a squadron of five Valerians, headed by a **red *"squad leader"* copter**, will fly in a line and make strafing runs at the enemy.

**This endpoint is deprecated and planned to potentially be removed by December 2023. It is recommended to switch to [v3](/wiki/API_v3_(GraphQL) "API v3 (GraphQL)") of the API.**

## **Overview**

The Alliance Members API can be used to access information about your alliance's member information. It displays information found in the Alliance Control panel, along with extra information. Use of this API requires your API key.

### **Access URL**

```
baseurl/alliance-members/?allianceid={id}&key={api key}
```

### **Alliance Member Resource Information**

Nations in alliances have a setting on the account page to prevent alliances from having access to their money and resource information. If they prevent access, values returned by the API for all money and resources are **-1**.

## **Returned JSON**

With the following request

```
accessurl/?allianceid=790&key=897sfn72e7xhh0u
```

[![Space Program](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/f/f8/Space_Program.png/revision/latest?cb=20200129222349)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/f/f8/Space_Program.png/revision/latest?cb=20200129222349) 



 

Space Program is a [National Project](/wiki/National_Project "National Project") that enables the construction of further space-related national projects such as [Spy Satellite](/wiki/Spy_Satellite "Spy Satellite"), [Telecommunications Satellite](/wiki/Telecommunications_Satellite "Telecommunications Satellite"), [Moon Landing](/wiki/Moon_Landing "Moon Landing") and [Mars Landing](/wiki/Mars_Landing "Mars Landing"), as well as [Green Technologies](/wiki/Green_Technologies "Green Technologies"). The Space Program also allows your nation to construct up to 3 [Missiles](/wiki/Missiles "Missiles") per day (instead of the base rate of 2 / day with the [Missile Launch Pad](/wiki/Missile_Launch_Pad "Missile Launch Pad") National Project.)

To build this project you need 20,000 Uranium [![Uranium](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/3/31/Uranium.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416051754)](/wiki/Resources#Natural_Resources "Uranium"), 20,000 Oil [![Oil](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/0/06/Oil.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416051531)](/wiki/Resources#Natural_Resources "Oil"), 10,000 Iron [![Iron](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Natural_Resources "Iron"), 5,000 Gasoline [![Gasoline](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Gasoline"), 1,000 Steel [![Steel](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Steel"), 1,000 Aluminum [![Aluminum](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Aluminum") and $40,000,000.

title: Gross National Income
content:
**Gross National Income** (**GNI**) is a nation's annual economic output less the market value of resources being imported and consumed. GNI allows for a good apples-to-apples comparison of economic status between nations. For example, if your GNI is $100,000,000, that means that over the course of 1 year your nation (at current rates & market values) is producing $100,000,000 worth of money and resources.

## Formula

GNI = Monetary Net Income \* 365

## See also

* [Gross Domestic Product](/wiki/Gross_Domestic_Product "Gross Domestic Product")

The **Propaganda Bureau** is a [National Project](/wiki/National_Project "National Project") that increases your military unit recruitment rate. Propaganda Bureau increases the number of Soldiers, Tanks, Aircraft and Ships you can recruit per day by 10%. It does not increase your caps on these units, or affect Missile, Nuclear Weapon or Spy production.

To build this project you need 1,500 Aluminum [![Aluminum](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/ba/Aluminum.png/revision/latest?cb=20150416044855)](/wiki/Resources#Manufactured_Resources "Aluminum") and $15,000,000.

title: Ground Battles
content:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Tools blue.svg](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/2/2d/Tools_blue.svg.png/revision/latest?cb=20150213023616) | This page is about game mechanics. This page is about game mechanics. It contains information such as formulas, costs, & other miscellany. See [Category:Mechanics](/wiki/Category:Mechanics "Category:Mechanics") for other pages on game mechanics. |

## Overview

Ground battles are the most basic attack in war. They use 3 Military Action Points (MAPs), so you can gather enough MAPs for up to 4 ground battles per war in 24 hours. Ground battles use [tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks") and [soldiers](/wiki/Soldiers "Soldiers"). To launch a ground battle, you need to have at least 50 soldiers on the offensive.

Your victory level determines how much money you can steal, how much resistance your opponent will lose, and the amount of damage done. If you achieve an immense triumph ground battle victory, you remove 10 Resistance and have a 10% chance of destroying an enemy improvement (excluding power plants).

To build soldiers and tanks, you need barracks and factories respectively. Soldiers fight more effectively with munitions and tanks require both munitions and gas to be used (both in offensive and defensive battles).

## Ground Control

Ground battles may result in you or your opponent obtaining ground control. Achieving an Immense Triumph in a Ground Battle will result in you obtaining ground control over your opponents. Once Ground Control has been established, all subsequent Ground Battles will destroy some of your opponent's Aircraft (based on the number of Tanks you send in battle.)

## Loot

Successful ground battles will result in money being stolen from the opponent, assuming they have money that can be stolen. The function which determines the amount of money stolen is dependent upon the number of attacking soldiers, tanks, the attacking nation's war policy, the defending nation's war policy, and the war type.

Defined in terms of variables, the formula which determines the maximum amount of loot stolen is:

SoldiersStolenMoney = Attacking Soldiers \* 1.1

TanksStolenMoney = Attacking Tanks \* 25.15

MaximumRandomFactor = 1.1

WarTypeFactor = 1

Note: If the war type is Ordinary, the WarTypeFactor = 0.5 and if the war type is Attrition the WarTypeFactor is 0.25

WarPolicyFactor = 1

Note: If the defender's war policy is [Moneybags](/wiki/Moneybags "Moneybags") the WarPolicyFactor is 0.6. If the attacker's war policy is [Pirate](/wiki/Pirate "Pirate") the WarPolicyFactor is 1.4. If both of these war policies are applicable, they cancel each other out and the WarPolicyFactor = 1

VictoryFactor = 3

MaxMoneyStolen = (SoldiersStolenMoney + TanksStolenMoney) \* VictoryFactor \* MaximumRandFactor \* WarTypeFactor \* WarPolicyFactor

### Practical Limitations

In practice, the maximum loot possible is not likely to be the amount stolen in a ground battle. In reality, the MaximumRandomFactor is actually a random number generated in the range [0.8,1.1], and the VictoryFactor is determined by the type of war outcome (0 = Utter Failure, 1 = Pyrrhic Victory, 2 = Moderate Success, 3 = Immense Triumph).

Additionally, there are limitations set by how much money the target nation has. For example, you cannot steal more than 75% of the defending nation's cash on hand, nor can you steal their last $1,000,000.

## Infrastructure Damage

The amount of damage done by a ground battle is dependent upon a number of factors.

The base formula for infrastructure damage is:

Infrastructure Destroyed = MAX( MIN((Attacking Soldiers - (Defending Soldiers \* 0.5) \* 0.000606061 + (Attacking Tanks - (Defending Tanks \* 0.5)) \* 0.01) \* RAND(0.85,1.05) \* (Victory Type / 3), City's Infrastructure \* 0.2 + 25), 0)

War Type and War Policy factors are multiplied to the base damage calculation. Victory Type is 0 for Utter Failure, 1 for Pyrrhic Victory, 2 for Moderate Success, and 3 for Immense Triumph.

## Casualties

Note: A defending nation will have a resisting population added to their army strength, which is equal to `population/400`.

Army Value = Unarmed Soldiers \* 1 + Armed Soldiers \* 1.75 + Tanks \* 40  
ATSR = rand between 40% and 100% attacking soldier army value  
DTSR = rand between 40% and 100% of defending soldier army value  
ATTR = rand between 40% and 100% of attacking tank army value  
DTTR = rand between 40% and 100% of attacking tank army value  
AR = total attacking army value random roll  
DR = total defensive army value random roll

If AR > DR then Attacker Tank Casualties += (DTSR \* 0.0004060606) + (DTTR \* 0.00066666666)  
If AR > DR then Defender Tank Casualties += (ATSR \* 0.00043225806) + (ATTR \* 0.00070967741)  
If AR <= DR then Attacker Tank Casualties += (DTSR \* 0.00043225806) + (DTTR \* 0.00070967741)  
If AR <= DR then Defender Tank Casualties += (ATSR \* 0.0004060606) + (ATTR \* 0.00066666666)  
Attacking Soldier Casualties += (DTSR \* 0.0084) + (DTTR \* 0.0092)  
Defending Soldier Casualties += (ATSR \* 0.0084) + (ATTR \* 0.0092)

There are 3 rolls per battle. So to calculate min casualties you would assume lowest possible roll every time, for max the opposite

The Felgrand Order is a white alliance founded on March 3, 2020, by the Lord Marquis Arthfael of Deheubarth.

## The Government of Felgrand Order

### Governmental Structure

Felgrand Order is a Parliamentary monarchy without an elected parliament. The Parliament consists of the Lord Marquis's appointed Paladins that advise the Lord Marquis and vote on propositions made by the other Paladins.

### Governmental Ranks

The Felgrand Order has 3 levels in its governmental hierarchy, Lord Marquis, Grand Marquis and Paladin. Paladins are assigned a department, led by a Grand Marquis.

## History

Although the history and early days of the order are shrouded in mystery, there is a rumour about that a certain Super Cool Awesome Pink Ranger has been guarding and protected the people of the order since its inception.

As of the 19th October 2020, Felgrand Order has been merged with Purgatory to form The [Dual Suns](/wiki/Dual_Suns "Dual Suns").

The **Pollution Index** of a city indicates how polluted your city is. Pollution is increased by most improvements. Each pollution point increases your disease rate by 0.05%. Recycling Centers and Subways reduce your pollution index.

## Effect on Disease Rate

Pollution causes the disease rate of a city to increase in a linear fashion. This results in a corresponding reduction in total population.

:   Disease Increase = ( .05% ) \* ( Pollution Points )

Whenever a Victory is obtained in a Ground Battle during a war, there is always a chance of looting money off the opposing nation. If the nation is defeated (gets its Resistance to 0) it loses resources as well as money.

* Whenever you perform a ground battle you have a chance to loot the enemies money, however if they have less than $50,000 times the number of their cities, no money is looted.
* Once you defeat an enemy you loot 10% of their cash and each resource they have, excluding credits.

**This endpoint is deprecated and planned to potentially be removed by December 2023. It is recommended to switch to [v3](/wiki/API_v3_(GraphQL) "API v3 (GraphQL)") of the API.**

The bank API can be used to access information about an alliance's bank that you have permissions for.

## Accessing the API

The Bank API can be accessed at the URL:

```
baseurl/alliance-bank/?allianceid=X&key=Y
```

*The X should be the alliance ID you want to access. The Y should be your API key, it is a hexadecimal key which can be found at the bottom of your account page in-game.*

Successfully inputting the above, you'll get the bank information returned as JSON. Otherwise:

If you input a valid API key but not an alliance that you have access to you'll get this:

```
{
    "success":false, 
    "general_message":"Unable to access. You are not in this alliance." 
}
```

If you input a false API key you'll get this as a response:

```
{
    "success":false,
    "general_message":"Invalid API key." 
}
```

An example of a call to this API should look like this:

<http://politicsandwar.com/api/alliance-bank/?allianceid=3940&key=a3bf9fdb8f39a1>

Obviously, that's not an actual API key, just an example.

title: Fundamentals of Gameplay
content:
[![Wiki-wordmark](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/8/89/Wiki-wordmark.png/revision/latest?cb=20131229234429)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/8/89/Wiki-wordmark.png/revision/latest?cb=20131229234429)

This is a basic explanation of the game provided by Sheepy (and may have been revised by other users) intended for new players trying to get a quick overview of how the game works. Many alliances will have a more up to date guide than this and may offer additional assistance, so it is highly recommended you join an established alliance.

So you've just created your nation, you're looking at your nation page, now what? Here's the basic breakdown.

## Cities

:   *Main article: [City](/wiki/City "City")*

Your nation is a collection of cities which you have control over. There's a [City](/wiki/City "City") page that does somewhat more in depth than what this guide is going to cover right now. You may view your cities using the [Sidebar Menu](/wiki/Sidebar_Menu "Sidebar Menu") to the Cities page within the game. So you know that cities make up your nation, what makes up cities?

### Infrastructure

:   *Main article: [Infrastructure](/wiki/Infrastructure "Infrastructure")*

What's infrastructure? By definition, it's the basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g. buildings, roads, and power supplies) needed for the operation of a society. Infrastructure directly increases your population by 100 per level. You can think of it as a *positive* population factor.

### Land

:   *Main article: [Land](/wiki/Land "Land")*

Land is how much room is available within your city. You need to be careful not to let it be too low, not much land and a lot of infrastructure will give you a high [population density](/wiki/Population_Density "Population Density"). Too high of population density means your citizens are congested and very prone to [disease](/wiki/Disease "Disease").

### Improvements

:   *Main article: [Improvements](/wiki/Improvements "Improvements")*

Improvements are special additions to cities with various effects. You can purchase one improvement for every 50 infrastructure you have in your city. Some improvements require your city to have **power**, which is supplied via **Power Plants**, a type of improvement. Just starting out **resource extraction** improvements are your best bet. You can produce those without power and sell them on the market to bring in extra money and grow your nation.

### Population

:   *Main article: [Population](/wiki/Population "Population")*

Toying around with infrastructure and land will make it pretty clear that your population can vary wildly. As mentioned before, infrastructure is a *positive* population factor. There are a few other factors that come into play.

#### City Age

As your city gets older, the population will slowly grow each day regardless of infrastructure. This is another *positive* population factor. The age of a city increases its population by a percentage.

#### Crime

:   *Main article: [Crime](/wiki/Crime "Crime")*

Crime is a *negative* population factor. The higher your crime rate, the more people are subtracted from your "positive" population value. [Crime](/wiki/Crime "Crime") is based upon the [average income](/wiki/Average_Income "Average Income") and population of your city. Average income is low, your crime rate will be higher, and an increase in population will increase your overall crime rate. Crime is something that only medium to large sized nations will need to worry about, as a new nation it's negligible.

#### Disease

:   *Main article: [Disease](/wiki/Disease "Disease")*

Disease is a very important *negative* population factor. Disease is caused primarily by having a high population density. If you buy a lot of **Infrastructure** you might see your disease rate go up to 100% and see your population drop to 10. Simply buying some land will decrease the **population density** and end your disease problem. Larger nations may purchase hospital improvements to lower disease in a city.

#### Pollution

:   *Main article: [Pollution](/wiki/Pollution "Pollution")*

Pollution Index measures how polluted your city is. Pollution is caused by most improvements. Each pollution point increases your disease rate by 0.05%. Recycling centers and Subways reduce your pollution index.

### Commerce

:   *Main article: [Commerce](/wiki/Commerce "Commerce")*

While this shouldn't be important to new nations, this guide will touch on it briefly. There are commerce improvements like Banks which increase your commerce level and thus your average income within the city. This will help drop the [crime rate](/wiki/Crime "Crime") and bring in more tax revenue.

#### Average Income

The range of average income available in the game goes from $2.50-$7.50. This value is per day, however you get income from your citizens every 2 hours automatically. By default your average income will be $2.50. Increasing average income is something intended primarily for larger nations, as a new nation it will cost less to start by mining resources and selling them to larger nations in demand of them.

## Trade

Trade is a major international activity. There are 6 continents in the game and each has 3 out of 6 varying resources. Learn more about resources by visiting the [Resources](/wiki/Resources "Resources") page.

### Selling Resources

Early on, it is recommended that you check out the market and see what resources are in demand and their prices are. Investing in production of a resource that is in demand at a good price will bring in extra income which will help you grow.

## Wars

For the first 14 days after your nation is created no one will be able to declare war on you. You will, however, be able to declare wars on other players. Declaring war on an enemy will end your 14 day protection. For this reason, it is not recommended that you do this, and take the extra time to boost your nation to a point where you can buy a basic military.

### War Ranges

You will only be able to declare on nations that are 67% higher than you in score or 34% below you. This will prevent you, a brand new nation, from fighting a "world power" sized nation.

### Defending Yourself

Even though you will only be facing opponents of your size, if any, it is advised you keep some soldiers on hand to protect yourself if necessary. If you get caught off guard without any military protection it will be easy for an opposing nation to begin to destroy infrastructure in your cities while stealing money and resources.

#### Barracks

Barracks are basic improvements that will allow you to maintain up to 3,000 [soldiers](/wiki/Soldiers "Soldiers"). You will be able to enlist up to 1/3 of your maximum per day, so if you have one barracks you would be able to produce 1,000 soldiers per day until you reached 3,000 soldiers. It is recommended that sometime on your 3rd day of playing you take some money and invest in a power plant in your capital city and get a barracks. Then train 1,000 troops that day and keep them standing by in case someone attempts to attack you.

## Alliances

Alliances are player created and lead organizations of nations that work together for mutual cooperation. They usually have a leader to represent them and use their own off-site forums to organize. You may receive recruitment messages from one or more alliances inviting you to join them. Additionally, there is an [Alliance Recruitment Subforum](http://politicsandwar.com/forums/index.php?/forum/16-recruitment-threads/) that contains threads from different alliances with information about them and why you should be interested in joining. Most alliances offer protection from attackers, better trading opportunities (such as better rates), financial aid, and most likely a better starting guide than this one.

## Miscellaneous

Here are a few more things to be aware of that don't necessarily fit into any of the other topics so far.

### Game Forums

The game forums are an excellent source of additional knowledge and discussion. There's a [Game Discussion](https://politicsandwar.com/forums/index.php?/forum/51-game-discussion/) forum where you can ask about things you're not sure about. If you find anything wrong with the game, there's a [Tech Support](https://politicsandwar.com/forums/index.php?/forum/48-tech-support/) forum as well. Additionally, if you have any good ideas there's a [Game Suggestions](https://politicsandwar.com/forums/index.php?/forum/52-game-suggestions/) forum too, along with much more. Take a look at the [forums](http://politicsandwar.com/forums/) and see if there's anything you're interested on there.

title: VIP

A VIP Subscription makes your account recognizable as a supporter of Politics & War, and offers a variety of special benefits. Benefits of being a VIP Member include:

* a VIP badge on your nation page
* a custom nation background
* a custom cover image
* custom city images
* the ability to choose a national anthem that is displayed on your nation page
* having a custom portrait image appear on your nation in-game

A VIP Subscription costs 1 credit per 60 days.

title: Soldiers
content:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Tools blue.svg](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/2/2d/Tools_blue.svg.png/revision/latest?cb=20150213023616) | This page is about game mechanics. This page is about game mechanics. It contains information such as formulas, costs, & other miscellany. See [Category:Mechanics](/wiki/Category:Mechanics "Category:Mechanics") for other pages on game mechanics. |

 [![Soldiersmall](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/b1/Soldiersmall.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/220?cb=20150411062026)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/b1/Soldiersmall.png/revision/latest?cb=20150411062026) 



 

**Soldiers** are basic units that are used in ground battles both offensively and defensively (the other unit used in ground battles are [tanks](/wiki/Tanks "Tanks")). They are key components to winning wars and battles. The amount of loot gained by victories depends of the number of soldiers you send – infrastructure destroyed is also determined by your battle results (immense triumph, moderate success, pyrrhic victory). You need one barracks for every 3,000 soldiers, and can only produce 1,000 soldiers per barracks each day.

Achieving an "immense triumph" on the ground will give the nation ground control, which restricts the enemy to using only 67% of their [aircraft](/wiki/Aircraft "Aircraft") .

## Cost

Troops are cheap units. They cost $5 per soldier to enlist. They have a daily upkeep cost of $1.25 and 1 ton of food per 750 soldiers. In war, however, they cost $1.88 per troop per day and 1 ton of food for 500 soldiers.

## Munitions

By default, soldiers will arm themselves with any available munitions, which are manufactured from lead. This increases their combat value by 75%, making them go from 1 combat value point (100% effectiveness) to 1.75 (175% effectiveness). You can choose for your soldiers not to use munitions, and they will fight at the normal effectiveness.

## Soldier Capacity

Soldiers are supported by Barracks which are military city improvements. Each Barracks can support a maximum of 3,000 Soldiers, and allows you to recruit up to 1,000 Soldiers per day.

### Population Support

Maximum soldier capacity is also limited by a nation's population. Your maximum soldier count cannot exceed 15% of your nation's population, regardless of how many Barracks you have.

This page is about game mechanics. It contains information such as formulas, costs, & other miscellany. See [Category:Mechanics](/wiki/Category:Mechanics "Category:Mechanics") for other pages on game mechanics. |

## Overview

 [![Land](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/a/a9/Land.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/210?cb=20170518095502)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/a/a9/Land.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170518095502) 



 

**Land** is a game mechanic that can be purchased in [Cities](/wiki/City "City"). It indicates how much space is available for your city.
Too little land and a lot of infrastructure will give you a high [Population Density](/wiki/Population_Density "Population Density"). Too high population density means your citizens are congested and very prone to [Disease](/wiki/Disease "Disease").

The more land you have in a city, the more food the farms of this specific city will produce. A farm produces 12 tons of food per day per 500 land. This is changed to 400 land with the [Mass Irrigation](/wiki/Mass_Irrigation "Mass Irrigation") national project.

You can find the cost of the land you want to purchase either by using the [Land Purchase Calculator](https://politicsandwar.com/tools/land) or by giving as input in one of your cities the amount of land you want to buy (click out of the field for the cost to appear and do not press enter or "Go" if you do not want to purchase the land).

title: Victory
content:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Tools blue.svg](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/2/2d/Tools_blue.svg.png/revision/latest?cb=20150213023616) | This page is about game mechanics. This page is about game mechanics. It contains information such as formulas, costs, & other miscellany. See [Category:Mechanics](/wiki/Category:Mechanics "Category:Mechanics") for other pages on game mechanics. |

## Overview

Victory is a war-related concept. Victory in a war ends the war and moves the defeated player to beige. It gives the defeated nation protection from new defensive wars, but existing wars may continue. To achieve victory, you must reduce your opponent's Resistance to 0.

The current fastest way of reducing resistance to 0 is by achieving 5 Naval Immense Triumphs, and 3 Ground Immense Triumphs.

Winning a war has 4 consequences;

1. The losing nation's color is changed to [beige](/wiki/Beige "Beige") for 2 days.
2. The nation's stockpiles of both money and resources are looted by the winner; 10% of money and 10% of all resources. Credits cannot be looted. These values are modified by War Type as well as [War Policy](/wiki/War_Policy "War Policy").
3. The nation loses up to 4% of infra in all cities; e.g. *x* city at 500 infra loses 20 infra, *y* city at 900 infra loses 36. This value is modified by War Type as well as [War Policy](/wiki/War_Policy "War Policy").
4. The alliance bank of the nation is looted, with the formula:

```
 MIN((Nation Score / Alliance Score)*R %, 33%)
```

where R = a random number between 0 and 1.

Here is an example of a victory message:

*Nation A won the war and looted $16,754, 77 Coal, 11 Oil, 19 Uranium, 68 Iron, 5 Bauxite, 15 Lead, 52 Gasoline, 242 Munitions, 31 Steel, 35 Aluminum, and 2,422 Food. Nation B also lost 4% of the infrastructure in each of their cities.*

See [Category:Mechanics](/wiki/Category:Mechanics "Category:Mechanics") for other pages on game mechanics. |

**Gross Domestic Product** (GDP) is a measurement of the wealth and resources generated by a nation over the period of one year. It is a cosmetic feature that has no gameplay effect, contrary to the Monetary Net Income figure that directly represents a nation's daily income.

## Wealth

GDP is determined in large part by a nation's gross income. Factors such as military and other expenses, as well as alliance taxes do not detract from a nation's GDP.

## Resources

The resources that a nation produces contribute to a nation's GDP, factored in at the current average market prices when GDP is calculated. For this reason, changes in average market prices can change the GDP of a nation, all other factors held constant. Resources refined or used to fuel power plants do not detract from a nation's GDP.

## GDP per Capita

GDP per Capita is the average GDP per citizen. A higher GDP per Capita generally indicates that a nation's citizens have a higher quality of life compared to a nation with a lower GDP per Capita.

## Calculation

GDP is the summation of a nation's gross income per day, as well as the monetary value of net resources produced, multiplied by 365.24. It is calculated and updated each time a nation visits its Revenue page.

## Formula

GDP = (Gross Income Daily + (Resources Produced Daily \* Average Market Prices)) \* 365.24  
GDP per Capita = GDP / Population

## How To Increase Your Nation's GDP?

You can increase your nation's GDP by increasing economic output in any way (increasing resource or refined goods production, increasing city commerce or population, etc.). Sometimes it is enough to simply maximize efficiency of your resource production, adjusting it for production bonuses and producing resources with higher market value.

## Leaderboard

The list of Top 10 Nations by GDP can be viewed at <https://politicsandwar.com/leaderboards/gdp>

## See also

* [Gross National Income](/wiki/Gross_National_Income "Gross National Income")

See [Category:Mechanics](/wiki/Category:Mechanics "Category:Mechanics") for other pages on game mechanics. |

## Overview

 [![Treasure](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/d/d9/Treasure.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170515133205) [![Treasure](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/d/d9/Treasure.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20170515133205)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/d/d9/Treasure.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170515133205) 



 

**Treasures** are a game mechanic that increases the income of the nations holding them as well as of the alliances to which these nations belong. There are 30 Treasures in total, scattered all over Orbis.

## Treasure Bonuses

Treasures provide two bonuses; a **Nation Treasure Bonus** and an **Alliance Treasure Bonus**.

 [![Treasurebonuses](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/6/68/Treasurebonuses.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170515121100) [![Treasurebonuses](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/6/68/Treasurebonuses.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/310?cb=20170515121100)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/6/68/Treasurebonuses.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20170515121100) 



 

* The **Nation Treasure Bonus** increases the income of the nation that holds a Treasure. Most treasures provide a 5% increase in the income of the nation due to this bonus, while there are 2 Treasures that provide a 9% increase. A nation having two or more Treasures gets a bonus from each and every Treasure.

* The **Alliance Treasure Bonus** is a game mechanic that rewards alliances that have nations which possess Treasures. When alliance members possess treasures in their nations, then ALL of the members of the alliance (except for alliance applicants and nations not on the same color as this of the alliance) receive this bonus. The Alliance Treasure Bonus is calculated by the following formula:

:   :   :   Alliance Treasure Bonus = sqrt(Treasures in Alliance \* 4)

It should be noted that a nation that holds a Treasure gets both the Nation Treasure Bonus and the Alliance Treasure Bonus, resulting in an increase of the nation's income of at least 7%.

## Acquiring a Treasure

There are three ways for a nation to acquire a Treasure; either a Treasure will spawn randomly in the nation or the nation will loot a Treasure from another nation or you can trade a treasure with another nation

* **Treasure Spawning:** Each Treasure automatically respawns in a new nation every 60 days. Each Treasure may spawn in nations of a specific color or continent (see next section for these spawning requirements). On top of the color and continent requirements, there is one more restriction that applies: Treasures spawn in nations whose [Nation Score](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Nation_Score) is within a specific range, i.e. anywhere from 15% to 65% of the Highest Nation Score in Game. The reason for the score range is to keep new, potentially inactive nations from receiving the treasures and to promote war in higher tiers where it's less common.

* **Treasure Looting:** Treasures are not commodities and can only be transferred through war. When you defeat (beige) a nation at [War](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/War)  (get its Resistance to 0), you take one of its treasures at random. The timer of the Treasure (time till its next respawn) is **not** reset.

* **Treasure Trading:** You can also trade treasures for money [here](https://politicsandwar.com/nation/trade/treasures/). This will directly give you the treasure if you are buying or give someone else the treasure you have.

Once a nation acquires a Treasure, the Treasure's icon will appear at the nation's page. There is no limit to how many Treasures a nation or alliance can have. The distribution of the Treasures among the nations of Orbis can be found in an in-game [leaderboards page](https://politicsandwar.com/leaderboards/display=treasures) displaying all of the treasures and who owns them.

## Treasures Description

In total, there are 30 Treasures. 10 of them are simple minerals, whereas the rest of them are Treasures inspired by real-life historical or mythological artifacts. There are 2 Treasures for each one of the 14 nation colors available (not counting grey and beige) and 2 Treasures that can spawn in nations with any kind of color (yet again, excluding grey and beige). Also, there is 1 Treasure for each one of the 6 continents, while the rest of the 24 Treasures may spawn in any continent.

title: S1 Series Main Battle Tank
content:
## S1 Ulster

[![20180510 104628](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/e/e8/20180510_104628.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180510145103)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/e/e8/20180510_104628.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20180510145103 "20180510 104628")


Marine Corp S1A1 supported by Viper Corp F/A-18

### Manufacturer

Sharp Industries

### Type

Main Battle Tank

### Size

Width: 11 feet (3.3 meter)

Height: 9 feet (2.7 meter)

Length (Without Gun): 25 feet (7.62 meters)

Length (With Gun): 36 feet (10 meters)

### Feed System

Auto-loader

### Cartridge

SIS-1082 Armor Piercing Shell

### Operation

600 k/m or 372.82 miles

### Rate of Fire

S1: 12 shells per minute

S1A1: 15 shells & 4 Missiles per minute

### Affiliation

Republic Federation Army

Republic Federation Marine Corp

### **- Overview**

The S1 Ulster is the first Tank designed and created in the [United Republic Federation](https://politicsandwar.fandom.com/wiki/Republic_Federation_of_States), used by both Army and Marine Corps. No exports are currently planned for the Three MBT models.

The Tank was given S1 as the original and the S1A1 as the upgraded variant, and the S1A2 as the Final Variant. With over 3,750 tanks produced, the MBT was able to fill in the additional slots along with giving the Military an advanced piece of hardware.

The Tank was first used during the Evan's Rebellion, then was used in mass by during the Foltest Wars. The simple repairs and maintenance made it possible for reuse.

### - **Design**

As the K1A1, M60 and the T-72 tanks come in, the Armed Company was producing thousands of copies for both the Army and the Marines to use. They even took the F-4 Phantom and redesigned it with F100 engines, reducing cost.

Knowing this, the Sharp Industries plans to design an indigenous tank to show off the company's ability to produce their own equipment and mass produce them with perfect quality and quantity.

After studying the K1A1 smoothbore gun, the head design was a redesign of the K1 Tank with some additional items added. The body of the T-72 tank was remade with some changes and modifications, along with its treads using hard rubber instead of metal. Creating the perfect tank they wanted, the XS1-01 and 02.

The "S" on the tank's designation represents the company's first letter of their name. This also shows that the Sharp Industries did create the tank.

Once the prototypes was ready, both tanks was tested against three K1A2s and four T-72Sims. The tanks then went head to head with the K1s, disabling them by shooting before the K1 tanks. Then putting it up against the T-72 tanks, using their Autoloader to their advantage. The only downside to the test, were the jamming of the Autoloader.

 [![URF Marine S1A1 MBTs traversing through the plains in Havenville, URFS](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/b5/S1_MBT_in_Plains.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/324?cb=20210723102314)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/b/b5/S1_MBT_in_Plains.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20210723102314) 

URF Marine S1A1 MBTs traversing through the plains in Havenville, URFS

 

The S1 Tank series was soon put into a recommended redesign. The plan was to give it better engine performance, better firepower, better armor, and higher production to retire both T-72Sim and M60A5 tanks. They will also complement the S1A1s, as those models were given an upgraded hull for a newer engine. An A2 variant was developed to give it a normal All Terrain Style, advance Infantry and Armored Support capabilities.

A design was planned with a callsign, A3 Final Series. The MBT was sent out the factory with: 1 x 55 .cal Autocannon, 2 x 7.62mm Anti-infantry machine gun, a 125 mm upgraded Berserker Rifle, and 1 x 30 mm Grenade launcher.

This makes it a multipurpose tank, giving it a anti-infantry and anti-armor weaponry. They then gave it a auto-target system for the machine gun and infrared-red systems to detect stealth vehicles, making it difficult to hide from the new tank. But the Tank was deemed too expensive and repetitive for Federation Forces, resulting in a cancellation of the program. The upgrades were given to A1, who are codenamed A1FU (Federation Urban).

They also gave the latest A1 and A2 models Super Turbo engine, pushing 2,200 - 2,500 horsepower into the vehicle. This makes it goes up to 65 mph, enabling the tank to actually drive on the Interstate Freeway. At the same time, this allows the tank to do hit and runs against other Armored Vehicles. The Gunner seat for the Machine Gun was given a protective glass canopy, keeping the Gunner alive and protected during Urban warfare.

The Sharp Industries has produced over 3,750 S1 Main Battle Tanks from 2019 till 2035, producing over 2,260 for the A1, A2, and Special variants. As each Division are deployed, M60s were decommissioned or put into training units. By 2033, Half of the original S1 MBTs were put into storage.

### - **Combat Service**

The Tank was put to the test as 200 S1 Tanks was sent into battle against Rebel Forces, succeeding against all enemy tanks as they attack them. Several Tank battles took place across Occupied Territory, mostly against advanced tanks that never thought up before. But each battle ended with the S1 MBT walking out unscathed.

They were soon put into combat in the late years of the [Foltest Wars](/wiki/Foltest_Wars "Foltest Wars"), going against tanks that scrapped both T-72s and K1A1 tanks easily. One Officer recounted a Battle when his S1 Tank took a hit, "We were under heavy fire, the enemy Tank targeted us after they massacred our footmen, but when he fired, the Tank continued on like it was nothing" he claims.

Once the War was over, the Tanks grew in numbers reaching to 1,000 vehicles. Having them split between the Army and the Marines. During the late years Foltest Wars, Federation Tanks used their advance repair capabilities to stay in the fight. Making them very dependable tanks during the entire conflict.

 [![S1A1FU Urban Tanks training with the URF Army 5th Armored Corp](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/a/ad/S1A1FU.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/178?cb=20210723102609)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/a/ad/S1A1FU.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20210723102609) 

S1A1FU Urban Tanks training with the URF Army 5th Armored Corp

 

In 2030, the upgraded S1A1FU and newer S1A2 Tanks are deployed to Argentina. As part of the Intervention of the Argentine Civil War, over 280 Tanks along with 700 K1A2FM are sent with the 25,000 Force. Their most famous actions were in the Eastern Coast of Argentina, where Area CDR. Lucas Thomas advanced near the ocean.

From August 17th - 30th, the Tanks gain over 490 Armored kills and 3,500 Infantry kills. They often are supported by Viper Operatives, Marines, and/or Regular Infantry, along with air support from URF Attack Helicopters or Fighter jets. They only faced a few losses mostly by Rebel Infantry, but the upgraded tanks perform well enough for URF Military Standards.

After the war, the upgrades and modifications are given to some S1 vehicles. While those vehicles are given their upgrades, other tanks are stored as replacements.

By 2033, almost a good portion of the Army and Marine Corp S1A1, S1A1FU, and S1A2 inventory were deployed to [West Africa](/wiki/West_African_War "West African War"). Most were sent into Nigeria to engaged Borno T-55M and T-62 tanks, eventually were redeployed to Lago Territory against Abrizhouian T-72 and M60 tanks. They also will fight against Royal Abrizhouian Guard's Challenger II tanks, breaking the backbone of Abrizhouian's Armored Corp.

In 2035 - 2038, almost all available models were deployed against Allied Imperial Forces. Fighting on all fronts, from Iceland to Siam to Quebec City itself. Used along side the K1A2, K1A3, T-72Sim2, and Viper Corp K2 Atlay tanks, They lead much of the campaigns across the world. The variants are also modified and deployed during the Korean Campaign, when S5A2 Artillery Tanks shelled military positions in the Korean city of Gwangju. They're also deployed a year later in Siam, shelling the 10 mile mark between Allied Forces and Siam Army positions.

### - **Specifications**

|  | S1A0 MBT | S1A1 MBT | S1A2 MBT | S1A1FU MBT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Commissioned Date | June 2026 | March 2028 | May 2030 | July 2030 |
| Produced | 1,490 (750 in-storage) | 1,500 | 560 | 200 |
| Weapons | - 110mm Hawkeye Rifle - 1x 50.cal (Coaxial) Machine Gun  - 1x (Top-Mounted) 7.62mm Machine Gun | - 120mm Smoothbore Gun - 50.cal (Coaxial) Machine Gun  - 30mm (Top-Mounted) Multiple Launcher Pod  - 1x (Top-Mounted) 7.62mm Machine Gun | - 145mm Berserker Smoothbore Rifle - 55.cal (Hull-Attached) Machine Gun  - 20mm (Side-attached) ATGM Launcher Pod  - 1x (Top Mounted) Glass-Canopy 7.62mm Machine Gun | - 125mm Prototype Berserker Smoothbore Rifle - 55. cal Coaxial Cannon  - 30mm (Top-mounted ) Automatic Grenade Launcher  - 7.62mm (Top-mounted) Glass-Canopy Machine Gun |
| System and Attachments | - Composite Armor (8 inches sloped front, 6 inches body) - Depleted Uranium/Steel Armor (Side-attached) | - Additional Armor with Hitpoint (10 inches sloped-front, 8 Inches body) - TUSK system (Attachable on All-Sides)  - Remote Controlled MG system | - Additional Armor with Hitpoint (12 Inches sloped-front, 9 Inches body) - TUSKA2 Armor -Trophy System Added | - Additional Armor with Hitpoints (10.5 inches sloped-front, 9 inches body) - Urban Defense System (Prototype Trophy Defense)  - Remote Controlled Weapon System |
| Engine | 1,950 hp Gas-Turbine | 2,000 hp Turbo Diesel-Turbine | 2,250 hp Turbo Electric-Turbine | 2,500 hp Prototype Turbo Electric/Diesel-Turbine |

| Weight | 50 tons | 55 tons | 55 tons | 60 tons |

## **Variants:**

### -**S2A0 MLRS:**

The S2A0 is a Multi Launch Rocket System on a S1 Ulster Chassis, this vehicle can carry up to 20 rockets and fire them in a wide area. For defensive purposes, it carries a 30mm Bushcannon and a 55 .cal Light Machine Gun. The only issue is the weight, going to a maximum 65 tons.

The Variant has began service during the West African War, deployed as part of a massive deployment of URF Forces. The Rocket system fired onto Insurgent positions, some units are used against Abrizhouian targets. All units were part of the last push against Boko Harem, acting as a scare tactic for Allied Forces against Insurgent Forces.

### **- S5A1 Artillery System:**

 [![S3A1 Artillery Tanks in Nashway, Ulster during training run.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/5/53/S3A1_SPG.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/115?cb=20200703014229)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/5/53/S3A1_SPG.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20200703014229) 

S3A1 Artillery Tanks in Nashway, Ulster during training run.

 

The S5A1 Artillery System is an Armored Self-Propelled Moblie Howitzer, the vehicle carries a 170mm cannon as the main armament. For defense, it carries a M60 Light Machine Gun. The range for the gun is up to 75km from it's position, along with precision aiming, makes it a dangerous vehicle.

Use of this vehicle began in 2027, but the most common appearance was in the West African War in 2034. Marines often used the vehicle over the MLRS or Mortars equipped to M1128 APCs, mostly to soften overrun positions.

### - **S4 Armored Recovery Vehicle**

The S4 ARV was used for transporting and repairing Armored Fighting Vehicles within the URF Ground Forces, first deployed in 2031 with the 3rd Armored Corp. They was soon deployed to Lagos as part of URF Military Response against Insurgents, supporting both Federation and Nigerian Armored Vehicles.

title: Trade History API
content:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [JSONicon](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/politicsandwar/images/3/3b/JSONicon.png/revision/latest?cb=20160321080623) | This page documents the API. This page is about the API for the game. It contains information such as contents, structure, & other miscellany. See [Category:API](/wiki/Category:API "Category:API") for other pages on the API. |

**This endpoint is deprecated and planned to potentially be removed by December 2023. It is recommended to switch to [v3](/wiki/API_v3_(GraphQL) "API v3 (GraphQL)") of the API.**

## **Overview**

The Trade History API provides information about the global trade history, requires an API key to operate.

### **Access URL**

```
baseurl/trade-history/key={api key}
```

This API cannot function without an API key being passed through it, it can be found at the bottom of the account page on the website.

## **Accepted Parameter(s)**

By default, it shows you the 1000 most recent trades for all resources, unless you pass the other accepted parameters to change the returned JSON.

The two parameters are:

* **resources** = the name of the resource you wish to filter for
* **records** = how many trades would you like to request

#### **Resources**

The list of acceptable resources can be find on the [Resources](/wiki/Resources "Resources") page, including credits. The names also have to be lowercase and are caps sensitive, so if a resource name isnt working double check if its both correct and is all lowercase.

```
accessurl&resources={resource name}
```

You can also filter for multiple resources at once:

```
accessurl&resources={resource name},{resource name},{resource name}
```

Unless this is passed then it will return the last 1000 trades for all resources, or however many records you requested for.

#### **Records**

```
accessurl&records={int}
```

Unless this is passed it will default to 1000. The minimum you can request for is 1 and the max being 10000.

#### **Using both parameters**

The order in which you pass the optional parameters does not matter but so both examples below are acceptable.

```
accessurl&resources={resource name}&records={int}
```

**OR**

```
accessurl&records={int}&resources={resource name}
```

## **Returned JSON**

Below is the JSON for the request of:

```
accessurl&resources=credits&records=2
```

```
{
    'success': True, 
    'trades': [
        {
                'trade_id': '4440588', 
                'date': '2018-12-17 15:29:12', 
                'offerer_nation_id': '141789', 
                'accepter_nation_id': '53361', 
                'resource': 'credits', 
                'offer_type': 'sell', 
                'quantity': '1', 
                'price': '12999999'
        }, 
        {'trade_id': '4440300', 'date': '2018-12-17 13:34:58', 'offerer_nation_id': '141789', 'accepter_nation_id': '115796', 'resource': 'credits', 'offer_type': 'sell', 'quantity': '1', 'price': '1299999'}
    ]
}
```

### **Error JSON**

Incorrect resource type:

```
{
        'success': False, 
        'general_message': 'No valid resource parameters were sent.'
}
```

Out of bounds records count:

```
{
        'success': False, 
        'general_message': 'Request is limited to 10,000 records maximum.'
}
```

**Emergency Gasoline Reserve** is a [national project](/wiki/National_project "National project") that boosts [Oil Refineries](/wiki/Improvements/Manufacturing "Improvements/Manufacturing")' production by 100% nationwide. Rates increase from 0.5/turn (per Oil Refinery) to 1/turn (per Oil Refinery). Oil usage is increased accordingly to create more Gasoline.

title: New Player Bonus
content:
The **New Player Bonus** is a percentage boost to gross income for nations with less than 21 cities. It is intended to make the game easier for new players, help them catch up, and hopefully, stick around. The bonus decreases as you buy more cities. At 21 cities, you no longer get any bonus.

| Gross Income Bonus | No of Cities |
| --- | --- |
| 100% | 1 |
| 95% | 2 |
| 90% | 3 |
| 85% | 4 |
| 80% | 5 |
| 75% | 6 |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
